title: Chicken Cacciatore
cScaleSummary: C4 because the recipe contains boneless skinless chicken thighs as the primary protein. Chicken thighs contribute more cholesterol than lean chicken breast, but the dish avoids butter, cream, cheese, egg yolks, sausage, bacon, and other concentrated cholesterol sources.
ldlActiveSummary: LDL Active is false because this recipe is built around chicken thighs as the primary protein. The recipe remains EWHF-appropriate because it is vegetable-forward, tomato-based, and uses olive oil instead of butter, cream, or cheese.
intro: Chicken cacciatore is a classic Italian hunter-style braise built from chicken, tomatoes, peppers, onions, mushrooms, garlic, wine, and herbs. This version keeps the rustic character of the traditional dish while using skinless chicken thighs, a vegetable-heavy sauce, and no butter, cream, or cheese.

stepGroups.title: Prepare and Brown the Chicken
items: Season the dried chicken with 1/2 teaspoon of {{ingredient:kosher-salt}} and {{ingredient:black-pepper}}.
Heat 1 tablespoon of {{ingredient:olive-oil}} in a large Dutch oven or deep skillet over medium-high heat.
Brown the seasoned chicken thighs for 3 to 4 minutes per side until well colored but not fully cooked through.
Transfer the browned chicken to a plate and reserve.

stepGroups.title: Build the Sauce
items: Add the remaining {{ingredient:olive-oil}} to the pan.
Add {{ingredient:cremini-mushrooms}} and cook for 5 to 6 minutes until browned.
Add {{ingredient:yellow-onion}}, {{ingredient:red-bell-pepper}}, {{ingredient:bell-pepper}}, and the remaining {{ingredient:kosher-salt}}.
Cook for 6 to 8 minutes until the vegetables soften and begin to caramelize.
Add {{ingredient:garlic}} and cook for 30 seconds.
Stir in {{ingredient:tomato-paste}} and cook for 1 to 2 minutes until slightly darkened.
Pour in {{ingredient:dry-red-wine}} and scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan.
Simmer for 2 minutes.

stepGroups.title: Braise the Chicken
items: Add {{ingredient:crushed-tomatoes}}, {{ingredient:chicken-broth}}, {{ingredient:dried-oregano}}, {{ingredient:dried-thyme}}, {{ingredient:red-pepper-flakes}}, and {{ingredient:bay-leaf}}.
Stir to combine.
Return the browned chicken and any accumulated juices to the pan.
Reduce the heat to low and partially cover the pan.
Simmer for 25 to 30 minutes until the chicken is tender and reaches 165°F in the thickest portion.

stepGroups.title: Finish and Serve
items: Remove the bay leaf.
If the sauce is thinner than desired, simmer uncovered for approximately 5 minutes until thickened.
Stir in {{ingredient:red-wine-vinegar}} and {{ingredient:fresh-parsley}}.
Taste and adjust with additional vinegar or black pepper if desired.
Serve hot.
